title: Post-launch readiness harness for VPC: API liveness, model warmup, incremental load
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an automated post-launch readiness harness that runs after Terraform applies a Private (VPC) deployment. The harness must validate API readiness, exercise model load paths, perform incremental smoke load tests, and produce machine-readable results for the console and CI. This ticket focuses on the orchestration glue: invoking Terraform outputs, running liveness/readiness probes, priming model KV cache and embeddings cache, running progressive concurrency ramps, and exporting pass/fail and metrics to the deployment report.
steps: 1) After terraform apply succeeds, extract outputs: terraform output -json | jq '.private_api_url.value' and '.instance_id.value'
2) Validate control-plane connectivity: curl --fail -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' $API_URL/health || fail
3) Run API readiness probe with retries (10 attempts, exponential backoff): GET /v1/status and /v1/models/list and assert expected model is present
4) Fetch model artifact metadata from deployment manifest and kick off a model warmup job via POST /internal/warmup with small prompt set (10 prompts) to populate KV cache
5) Run a model-load timing test (single-connection): record time-to-first-token and full load time; expect ttf < 45s for medium models on Dedicated-1 profiles

6) Incremental smoke load: ramp concurrent connections 1 -> 5 -> 20 over 6 minutes using the load harness (we use our internal load-generator image). Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and GPU memory util
7) KV/prefix cache validation: ensure repeated prompts hit caching paths by measuring delta in token-gen time after warmup
8) Resource checks: validate agent-level metrics via Prometheus endpoint (cpu < 70%, mem < 85%, gpu_mem < 92%) and that container restart count == 0
9) Export structured results as JSON to /var/deploy/reports/post_readiness.json and upload to console artifact store (s3://redwood-deployments/<env>/<id>/reports)
10) Fail fast policy: if API readiness or model presence checks fail, abort remaining steps and create an incident with links to logs and relevant terraform state
acceptance_criteria: H1: After terraform apply the harness runs automatically as a post-deploy step in CI or via the operator playbook
H2: API readiness endpoints return 200 within 2 minutes of service reachability for >= 95% of successful deploys
H3: Model warmup completes and reduces mean token generation time by >= 30% on repeated prompts
H4: Incremental smoke load at concurrency 20 results in error_rate <= 1% and p95 latency < 800ms for small/medium model families (document exceptions)
H5: The harness writes a machine-readable report containing status, p95/p99, ttf, GPU memory, and a pass/fail boolean
H6: Console picks up the artifact URL and surfaces a clear pass/fail badge on the deployment summary
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Scoped requirements with Product (Nora Li) — decided to keep post-launch harness as step in our terraform CI pipeline rather than a separate operator job to minimize drift.
2026-02-20: Spike completed for model warmup endpoints. Prototype warms KV with 10 prompts and shows 40% reduction in median token time on test infra (g4dn-like profile).

2026-02-23: Hooked into terraform outputs; used instance metadata + private api url. Found race where service registers model list ~20s after LB becomes reachable — added readiness polling with exponential backoff.

2026-02-27: Initial smoke harness (bash + golang runner) landed in repo. Running incremental load fails at concurrency 20 on smallest machine type — tuned batch window and decreased behind-the-scenes token batching to reduce latency spikes.

2026-03-02: Added structured JSON report format and S3 upload step. Open question: how to handle multi-model deployments (fan-out warmup) without long blocker times — propose configurable parallelism per deployment size.
comments: Arjun Patel (2026-02-18): Recommend adding an opt-out flag for very large model families to skip full warmup and instead run a lightweight liveness check.

Lucas Rivera (2026-02-24): Observed memory thrashing when running parallel warmups on two large models in the same node group — suggest serializing warmups by default and make parallelism configurable.
Nora Li (Product) (2026-02-25): PM note: push for a clear UX in Console that marks post-readiness failure as 'Requires Operator' when model warmup fails, rather than auto-roll-back.
Security (2026-02-26): Reminder to redact any PII or secrets in uploaded reports; use temporary presigned URLs for S3 artifacts.
